summary: KAUST (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology) in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia admits MS, MS/PhD and PhD students in science and engineering programmes from applicants worldwide. Every admitted student receives the KAUST Fellowship, so there is no separate scholarship application. The Fellowship covers tuition and bench fees, a yearly stipend, base accommodation, health insurance and relocation costs for the move to KAUST and the return home. Admission is competitive and based on documents, a faculty review and an interview.
eligibility_notes:
Education: MS applicants need a bachelor's degree, and PhD applicants a master's degree, in a subject relevant to the programme from a recognised higher education institution (the programme pages mention engineering, mathematics and the physical, chemical and biological sciences). A PhD can also be entered from a bachelor's degree (longer residency). Professional master's degrees are not treated as equivalent to master's degrees and must be declared. Some programmes may add an entrance exam or extra coursework.

Age and grades: at least 18 on entry. Minimum GPA 3.0 on a 4-point scale or equivalent; about 90 percent of admitted applicants have above 3.3 and 75 percent above 3.5. Admission is holistic, so scores are not the only factor.

English: an official test score is required even if you studied in English, and it must be met before enrolment (you may apply without one, but a score is strongly encouraged). Minimum: Academic IELTS 7 overall with at least 6.5 in each section; PTE Academic 71 with at least 67 in each section; Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 185 with at least 176 in each section. TOEFL iBT is accepted (the page lists figures that look inconsistent with the TOEFL scale, so confirm them with KAUST). TOEFL Home Edition and IELTS Online are accepted. Scores are valid for two years from the test date. Not accepted: medium of instruction certificates, the Duolingo test (except for visiting students), TOEFL MyBest superscores and IELTS One Skill Retake. Exempt: a degree completed in person at an accredited institution in the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand (distance learning, satellite or branch campuses and joint programmes do not count), or a previous degree from the KAUST campus in Thuwal. Saudi nationals and PhD students may be admitted with lower scores (IELTS 6.5 overall and 6 per section; PTE 64 and 61; Cambridge 176 and 169) if they take the Academic English Language Communication Course in their first semester. The page does not say whether non-Saudi master's applicants qualify for this route.

Tests: the GRE General Test and PGAT are optional and not required.

Funding rules: students sponsored by another university, company or other source can apply, but if admitted they do not receive the Fellowship on top of that sponsorship. Scholarships for extras such as conference travel or a computer do not affect eligibility; substantial external support for tuition, relocation or living costs must be declared. Students admitted through partnerships or sponsorships may have different benefits. The Fellowship does not cover English test fees. A second master's is only possible in rare cases; current graduate students are encouraged to go for a PhD. You may submit only one application at a time and to one programme per year.
age_experience_notes: Minimum age 18 on entry. The pages state no maximum age and no work-experience requirement. Professional referees are accepted only if your latest qualification was completed more than three years before applying.
funding_summary: The Fellowship covers tuition and bench fees (worth up to USD 35,000 a year), a stipend (USD 20,000 a year for MS students; USD 25,000 to 30,000 a year for PhD students depending on qualifications and progress), base accommodation, health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus, and relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel for the initial move and the return home after graduation. KAUST estimates the total value at USD 70,000 to 80,000 a year. The page does not state how many years funding lasts. For reference, the MS is a 36-credit programme normally done in three semesters plus one summer session (2 years for the thesis track as stated on one page); PhD residency is 3.5 years from a bachelor's and 2.5 years from a master's, with a maximum of five years, extendable. Average spending is about USD 1,320 a month, which KAUST says the stipend more than covers.
programmes_note: MS, MS/PhD and PhD degrees in science and engineering programmes; the study page states 17 MS subjects and the programmes-of-study page lists 16 programmes (full list below). Technology Innovation and Entrepreneurship is MS only. MS entry is Fall 2027 only; PhD entry is Spring 2027 (round 1 closed on 27 September 2026) and Fall 2027. MS applicants are not eligible for Spring 2027. Individual programmes may have additional requirements, so check the programme page.
institutions_note: All study is at KAUST in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. Students usually live in the Harbor, in units with private bedrooms and shared common areas and kitchens; family accommodation is available.

summary.detail: MS is a 36-credit programme normally taking three semesters plus one summer session; the thesis option takes about 2 years. Credits: core 9 to 15, electives 9 to 15, research or capstone 12; all 36 credits at graduate level. Thesis option: at least 6 credits of thesis research (12 expected), apply by the eighth week of the second semester, committee of the advisor plus two other faculty. Non-thesis option: at least 6 credits of directed research or one research-based summer internship. At least one full Winter Enrichment Program (each January) is required. An integrated MS/PhD pathway exists for bachelor's holders (typically 5 to 6 years). Fall entry only. Competition for MS places is high.

summary.detail: PhD residency is 3.5 years for bachelor's entrants and 2.5 years for master's entrants; maximum enrolment is five years, extendable with approval. Phases: qualifying exam (written research proposal accepted and a committee vote), oral defence of the dissertation proposal, then the dissertation with a final defence before a committee of four (at least three KAUST faculty and one external examiner). Students must advance to candidacy within 3 years (bachelor's entrants) or 2 years (master's entrants). Attendance at the Summer Session and Winter Enrichment Program is mandatory. Entry in Spring 2027 or Fall 2027.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition and bench fees fully covered, worth up to USD 35,000 per year
benefits.conditions: Some students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible; students sponsored by others do not receive the Fellowship in addition to the sponsorship. Detailed terms are given with the offer.

benefits.limit_text: Stipend of USD 20,000 per year for MS students; USD 25,000 to 30,000 per year for PhD students depending on qualifications and academic progress
benefits.conditions: KAUST says average student spending is about USD 1,320 per month, which the stipend more than covers.

benefits.limit_text: Base accommodation: shared for single students, 2-bedroom unit for married students; utilities are covered according to the cost-of-living page
benefits.conditions: Eligible students can request a housing upgrade for an additional fee.

benefits.limit_text: Health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus
Visa, relocation and travel costs for the initial move to KAUST and the return home after graduation only
benefits.conditions: No other travel is listed as covered; no caps are stated.

benefits.limit_text: English test fees are not covered
benefits.conditions: KAUST does not waive the English test requirement or pay for the test. Applying is free. A certified English translation of transcripts is arranged and paid for by the applicant unless the institution provides it.

requirements.text: Official transcripts from every institution attended, showing courses, credits (where applicable), grades, the final award and the grading scale. If your degree is incomplete, a partial or unofficial transcript, student records screenshot or other proof of progress is accepted at application, and an official final transcript is needed before enrolment. Non-English transcripts need the original and a certified English translation.

CV with full name as in your passport, date of birth, address, contact details, institutions and dates, qualifications (including pending), work experience, research and publications, and other skills and interests.
Statement of purpose of about 750 words.

Contact details of three referees with academic or professional email addresses (no personal emails); academic referees are expected. Requests are sent as soon as you enter the details, referees submit their references directly (you do not upload letters), and references are expected within seven calendar days of the deadline.
requirements.conditional_rule: Professional referees are allowed only if your most recent qualification was completed more than three years before applying

requirements.text: Official English test score (Academic IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic or Cambridge C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency), valid for two years; the minimum must be met before enrolment.
requirements.conditional_rule: Not needed with an in-person degree from the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, or a KAUST Thuwal degree

requirements.text: Clear copy of the passport photo page (Saudi applicants may give a national ID card instead). All supporting documents must be in English.
GRE General Test or PGAT official score report (valid 5 years). Optional; a strong score may help.
requirements.conditional_rule: only if you choose to submit one

application_steps.title: Choose one programme and check entry rules and dates
application_steps.detail: Pick one programme (only one application at a time and one programme per year; applying is free). MS and MS/PhD entry is Fall 2027 (application opened 28 September 2026 and closes 3 January 2027, per the page's tentative dates). PhD entry is also possible in Spring 2027 (round 1 deadline 27 September 2026, now passed).

application_steps.title: Prepare documents and enter your referees
application_steps.detail: Prepare official transcripts, a CV, a statement of purpose of about 750 words, a passport copy and any English score. Enter three referees' institutional email addresses in the portal; requests go out immediately and referees upload references themselves. You can list faculty you would like to work with but need not contact them first.

application_steps.title: Submit the application in the admissions portal before the deadline
application_steps.detail: Log into the application portal and submit before the round deadline. Applications cannot be changed after submission unless KAUST asks for more information. Check your status in the portal. Dates are tentative and may change with application volume.

application_steps.title: Admissions check, then faculty ranking
application_steps.detail: The Admissions team checks that documents are complete and contacts you about anything missing. Faculty then rank applications and shortlist the strongest candidates for interviews. Well-qualified candidates are forwarded to faculty, who may contact them.

application_steps.title: Online academic interview and/or test, then decision
application_steps.detail: Shortlisted applicants get an invitation to an online interview with faculty in their subject area covering academic background, interests and career goals. Decisions are sent by email (Fall 2027 round 2 decisions are planned for 25 February 2027). Decisions are final and KAUST gives no individual feedback.

application_steps.title: Accept the offer in the time given and read the Fellowship terms
application_steps.detail: If accepted you have a limited time to respond or the decision may be withdrawn. Detailed Fellowship terms come in the offer letter; there is no separate fellowship application. Declare any substantial external support. Meet the English minimum and provide the final official transcript before enrolment.

application_steps.title: Relocate, enrol and study
application_steps.detail: The Fellowship pays visa, relocation and travel for the initial move and the return home after graduation. The Fall 2027 semester starts on 29 August 2027. Students usually live in the Harbor and get a student handbook on arrival. MS students must complete at least one Winter Enrichment Program; PhD students must attend the Summer Session and Winter Enrichment Program.
